comparator.name: Dentistry (Tandheelkunde)
comparator.institution: University of Amsterdam through the Academic Centre for Dentistry Amsterdam (ACTA, a UvA-VU collaboration)
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026-2027 ACTA OER is the formally adopted source for the compulsory curriculum and confirms that ACTA is a collaboration of the University of Amsterdam and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. The official study guide confirms a three-year, 180-EC Dutch-taught bachelor. All listed units are compulsory and total 60+60+60=180 EC; there is no open elective space. Year 1 combines cells, tissues, organ systems, oral biology, cariology, microbiology, direct restorations, research methods and statistics, professional development, and two dental-skills lines. Year 2 combines prevention, care planning, immunology and pathology, cariology and periodontology, crowns, periodontitis, the medically complex patient, professional development, preparation for the scientific internship, dental prevention and two further dental-skills lines. Year 3 combines bridges, oral biology and periodontology, medically complex patients, evidence-based dentistry, a 14-EC scientific internship, endodontics, radiology, prevention/treatment and indirect-restoration clinical lines, professional development and professionally assessed conduct. The OER explicitly requires patient care and makes successful preclinical practical work a condition for treating patients. Independent UCR review on 2026-10-17 preserves this settled 2026-2027 reconstruction and its neutral generic route. Current ACTA programme pages corroborate prevention, patient wellbeing, communication and inclusive care, and ACTA still identifies the 2026-2027 OER as current. The direct OER PDF and study-guide portal were inaccessible during this review; their previously verified component list is preserved, without a new claim to have re-read the PDF. The recruitment overview now advertises 2027-2028; it does not supersede the applicable 2026-2027 curriculum.

alternatives.concept: Study cellular and systemic disease mechanisms, infection, immunity and pharmacology alongside epidemiology and psychological influences on health. Laboratory work, statistics and evidence synthesis support investigation of health and prevention. These sciences provide a related academic response to oral-health interests; oral biology, dental pathology, restorative techniques and clinical dental care remain substantial gaps.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum combines molecular and organ-system biology with epidemiology, psychology and health-research methods. It names this biomedical and health-science composition without implying that the selected courses teach oral biology or dentistry.

alternatives.concept: Examine health behaviour and patient experience through physiology, cognition, clinical and health psychology, and development across the lifespan. Sociology, qualitative research, ethics and public persuasion supply tools to investigate social circumstances, communication and access. This related academic direction does not teach dental examination, treatment planning, restorations or supervised patient care.

alternatives.labelRationale: Biomedical and psychological study forms the main curriculum. Cognitive impairment, social inquiry, ethics and persuasive communication contribute specifically to patient experience and health behaviour. The label does not imply dental treatment or specialist oral-health training.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Six courses / 45 EC differ in each direction. Molecular cell biology, biochemistry, infection/immunity, mechanisms of disease, molecular pathology and laboratory work give way to social psychology, perception/action, psycholinguistics, sociology, qualitative inquiry and persuasive communication. The curricular priority moves from biomedical mechanisms and laboratory evidence to cognitive, psychological and social processes shaping patients experience and health behaviour.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Biomedical and brain/behaviour gateways precede all dependent courses. Cell biology, physiology, biochemistry and anatomy precede advanced pathology and pharmacology where feasible. Research Methods & Statistics precedes experimental statistics and the meta-analysis seminar. Formal prerequisites and exact planned availability pass. Data handling occurs before final-year evidence synthesis. Abnormal Psychology is placed before Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies as a useful advisory progression.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two related academic responses were constructed sequentially. The further precise dental technology/restorative-design candidate (20620) was tested separately: Consumer Product Design teaches prototypes, materials, production and environmental impact, but no dental materials, oral mechanics, crowns, bridges, endodontics, dental imaging, preclinical simulation or operative dental skills. General design and autonomous systems cannot supply a complete coherent dental-technical programme. Oral-health promotion and wellbeing are already represented within the included prevention and patient-experience concepts; a separate prevention label would not generate a substantively different curriculum. Neither accepted programme is represented as a Dentistry substitute or a professional qualification.

Both address disease prevention. UCR epidemiology studies population risk and evidence rather than practical oral-disease prevention.
Both teach research design and statistics. UCR supplies general empirical methods rather than the dental-specific implementation.
Systematic review and meta-analysis directly contribute to evidence appraisal; the UCR seminar is not dental-specific evidence-based practice.

notes.text: ACTA Dentistry combines oral science, precise dental procedures and progressive supervised patient care. These UCR programmes offer biomedical health science or psychological and social study of health and patient experience. They do not reproduce oral biology, dental pathology, restorative procedures, preclinical dental skills or clinical dental training.
